text: 🇲🇽✊ "It's when the people win. Governments begin that govern for the people, not for the elite. That's the difference." "Political power is separated from economic power. (...) It's the right versus humanism, now even clearer." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 9, 2026 A reporter asked whether the real democratic alternation came in 2018, when López Obrador won with more than 30 million votes, and not in 2000. Fox recently admitted he helped Calderón win in 2006, and Labastida wrote that the 2000 transition was agreed with the US. Sheinbaum said nothing changed in 2000: since Salinas, the PRI and the PAN were one alliance, the "PRIAN", "one single vision of the country, which is the country of the past." Since 2018, she listed, there are well-being programs, minimum wage increases, more jobs, no inflation, a stable peso, and more than 13 million people out of poverty.

🔥🇲🇽 "The truth is this: Guadalupe Taddei was chosen by lottery in the Chamber of Deputies. Who voted for the five in that urn? All the political parties except one." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 9, 2026 Reporter Reyna Haydeé Ramírez played testimony from a member of the 2023 selection committee claiming the shortlist favored profiles close to Morena. Sheinbaum showed the vote: with no two-thirds majority, the law sends five finalists to a draw. The PAN, PRI, PVEM, PT, PRD and Morena approved the shortlist; only Movimiento Ciudadano voted against, and the PAN's Santiago Creel read out the winning name. Taddei, she said, came from the group formed under Lorenzo Córdova: "It could have been thought she was an honest person, but it turned out she wasn't." Anyone from any party who commits corruption must be punished.

🇲🇽⚖️ "No, cash is not going to be taken away. We're going to encourage, little by little, a greater number of digital payments." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 9, 2026 Asked about the new Digital Economy Law, which critics on Radio Fórmula called unconstitutional, Sheinbaum said nobody will be forced to pay digitally and stores keep taking cash. The one place where the government wants to eliminate cash completely is gas stations: together with fuel traceability, it helps end fuel theft and illegal fuel imports. Toll booths will move over gradually. She cited the Mexico City Metro, which switched from paper tickets to cards, and said its revenue went up. The Banco del Bienestar will soon present an app for direct payments.

🇲🇽✊ "This is the largest social participation program in health in the world." "Nobody knows the needs of a health center better than the community that uses those services every day." — Alejandro Svarch, head of IMSS-Bienestar, Mañanera, Nov 9, 2026 La Clínica es Nuestra 2026 starts this week: 8,797 IMSS-Bienestar health centers get between 400,000 and 1.2 million pesos each, paid directly on cards to the treasurers elected by local health committees, with no intermediaries. For the first time it includes all 153 health centers in Yucatán. In 2025, more than 67,000 committee members decided how to improve 8,483 centers. La Escuela es Nuestra reached 73,443 school communities this year with 23,320 million pesos, and 75.8% of all public schools in two years. Sheinbaum said it began in Mexico City as "Mejor Escuela."

🇲🇽🏭 "The US Fed raised its rate and the Bank of Mexico cut its rate, because it sees the Mexican economy performing well." "We're doing well, and we're going to do better." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mañanera, Nov 9, 2026 Mexico reached 23,088,353 formal jobs registered with IMSS in October, the highest figure in its history. That's 161,000 more than in September, 571,277 created so far this year, and 1.3% more than in October 2025. Sheinbaum said the government expected the second half of the year to be stronger because public works were starting, and that every economic indicator is now going well.

🇲🇽⚡ <u>CHICOASÉN II PASSES THE HALFWAY MARK</u>

President Sheinbaum toured the CFE's Chicoasén II hydroelectric plant in Chiapas on Sunday. It is 51.35% built, El Economista reports.

Three 80 MW turbines will add 240 MW of clean power using water that has already run through the Manuel Moreno Torres plant upstream, so the Grijalva generates twice. Expected reach: 54,241 homes and 184,421 people, plus 250 million pesos in social works for the municipality.

🇲🇽📚 <u>LA ESCUELA ES NUESTRA NOW REACHES 3 OUT OF 4 PUBLIC SCHOOLS</u>

In two years, the program has reached 141,025 of 185,972 schools, a 75.8% coverage rate. The money goes straight to parent committees, with no intermediaries and no contractors.

This year alone, 73,443 school communities have received funds, covering about 8.8 million students: 23.32 billion pesos delivered so far out of nearly 24 billion budgeted.

🇲🇽🇨🇺 <u>IN MADRID, MEXICO REJECTS THE US EMBARGO ON CUBA</u>

At the 30th Ibero-American Summit, Foreign Minister Roberto Velasco, speaking for President Sheinbaum, restated Mexico's historic position against the embargo and the coercive measures Washington imposes on Cuba.

On security, he set out Mexico's four principles with every nation: respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, shared but differentiated responsibility, mutual trust, and "cooperation without subordination."

He also reminded Spain of 1939, when Lázaro Cárdenas opened Mexico's doors to thousands of Republican refugees.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>UNDER CÓRDOVA, THE INE ALSO PAID THE "COYOTE" SUPPLIERS</u>

The Hernández Casillas network didn't start with Taddei. Contralínea found at least four INE contracts with the same companies under Lorenzo Córdova, now a councilor of the right-wing party Somos.

One of them, INE/ADQ-0022/15, went to Cartonera Plástica for the 2014–2015 election. It was tendered at 9.83 million pesos and ended above 11 million after a 1.44 million-peso add-on signed on April 8, 2015.

Sheinbaum has suggested the ASF audit go back to the 1990s. But sources told Contralínea that auditors in the state electoral bodies are only asking about Taddei's brief term.

🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO GRANTS ASYLUM TO NADIA BELLER, THE WOMAN AT THE CENTER OF THE CERIMEDO CASE</u>

Mexico's embassy in La Paz has granted diplomatic asylum to lawyer Nadia Beller, ex-partner of Fernando Cerimedo, the Argentine far-right digital strategist behind Milei's campaign. He has been jailed in Bolivia since August on attempted-femicide charges after gunmen attacked her.

Bolivia's foreign ministry confirmed it received Mexico's notice and safe-conduct request on November 4. Beller had denounced police harassment and a lack of guarantees for her safety.

The same embassy in La Paz sheltered Evo Morales's officials after the 2019 coup.
